calls.reason: The only evidence is OpenAI's o1 announcement. It can't show whether that made him 'eat crow' or made the spending 'worth it', and both standards are subjective.
Nvidia reported about $14.9B in quarterly net income and credited it to generative AI demand. Microsoft said AI added 7 points to Azure growth. Someone was clearly making money from generative AI.
EPRI's study covers all data centres and describes regional supply problems. It neither shows nor rules out a total national grid rebuild caused by generative AI.

The most concrete part, 'not generating any revenue', is flatly contradicted. OpenAI was on a $3.4B annual pace, Microsoft reported AI-driven Azure growth, and Nvidia reported record data centre sales.
The forecast has no deadline ('at some point'). Expanded Amazon, Google and Microsoft arrangements in 2026 show support continuing so far, but they can't settle an indefinite forecast.

OpenAI cut prices for comparable models about 3x in Nov 2023 and halved them again with GPT-4o in May 2024. Epoch's independent analysis found falling prices at fixed capability, not just thinner margins.
